My wife got tired of my screen addiction.
So she built an iOS app to fix me.
It worked.
9 hours of daily screen time → 5 hours in 2 weeks.
30 hours a week on social media. Gone.
The app is called Align: screen time blocker
What's your daily screen time right now? https://t.co/HXlxn5JbVe

Earned, not rationed. We built an iOS app that turns healthy habits — walking, reading, push-ups, hydration — into screen time minutes you unlock by verifying completion. Your attention was never free. Now you decide what it's worth.

Most of my PR’s in the last month have been shipped from my phone.

I built an iOS app that gives you a secure sandboxed cloud workspace so that you can work from anywhere. 

This is what cloning a repo, making a change, creating a PR and merging looks like.

Works with Claude, codex, cursor.

built an ios app
now building another b2b saas
while being a dad to a 5 month old baby girl

VCs call this “founder resilience”

my brain calls it “please sleep”

Cursor just shipped an iOS app — and it's wilder than it sounds.

SpaceX (yes, including xAI) acquired Cursor this month. A week later, the first iOS app drops. The timeline alone tells you this was a priority from day one post-acquisition.

Here's what the mobile app does:

- Launch coding agents from your phone
- Review diffs and merge PRs — inline, on an iPhone
- Annotate screenshots with visual feedback for agents
- Voice conversations with your coding agent
- Inspect code changes and track active engineering work
- Remote Control mode: run agents in the cloud, manage from your phone

Three things stand out:

1. This is the first credible "mobile-first" coding platform. Not a companion — a legit agent you control from your pocket.
2. SpaceX/xAI buying Cursor then immediately shipping iOS says everything about where they see the market going. Agents in the datacenter, interface in your hand.
3. 75% off Composer 2.5 runs through July 5 if you want to test it.

The blog post is honest: "The experience of running agents in the cloud will become indistinguishable from running them on your local machine." They're building toward a world where your coding agent lives in the cloud full-time and you interact from whatever screen is closest.

That's the endgame for agentic coding. Not a local IDE — a cloud agent with a mobile throttle.
